national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the population living on less than USD 8.30 per day, expressed in 2021 purchasing power parity (PPP) terms. This international poverty line, used by the World Bank, enables comparisons of poverty levels across countries and does not represent the national poverty line of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
national_rationale: Reducing poverty and social exclusion is a key objective of sustainable development. EU SDG indicator 1.10, “Persons at risk of poverty or social exclusion”, is based on data from the Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (SILC) survey. SILC data are not available in the Eurostat database for reporting this indicator for Bosnia and Herzegovina; therefore, values cannot be presented according to the harmonised EU methodology. Consequently, the World Bank’s proxy indicator is used. It measures the share of the population living below the international poverty line of USD 8.30 per day, expressed in 2021 purchasing power parity (PPP) terms. This indicator enables international comparisons but is not directly comparable with EU SDG indicator 1.10 and does not measure poverty against Bosnia and Herzegovina’s national poverty line.
national_methodology_characteristics: Data from the World Bank’s Poverty and Inequality Platform are available for selected years between 2001 and 2021. According to the available series, the share of the population living below the USD 8.30 per day threshold was 20.2% in 2001, 9.7% in 2004, 16.0% in 2007 and 2011, 17.3% in 2015, and 11.7% in 2021. Between 2015 and 2021, the share decreased by 5.6 percentage points. Given the limited frequency of the data and the proxy nature of the indicator, this change should be interpreted as a trend in the indicator’s value and not, on its own, as sufficient evidence for a reliable assessment of progress towards the official Sustainable Development Goal target.
national_long_objective: No specific quantitative national target has been established for this proxy indicator in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its interpretation should be based on the indicator’s definition and distinguished from national poverty-reduction measures and targets.
